title: The War Where Nobody Was Shot
description:
The Toledo War (1835-1836) was a boundary dispute between Ohio and the Michigan Territory over the Toledo Strip, a region at the mouth of the Maumee River. Poor geographical understanding of the Great Lakes had produced conflicting laws. Michigan's 24-year-old 'Boy Governor' Stevens T. Mason and Ohio's governor Robert Lucas both passed penalties against residents who submitted to the other side, and both sent militia to opposite banks of the river, where they mostly taunted each other. The only blood spilled was a non-fatal stabbing of a law enforcement officer. Congress offered Michigan statehood plus the remaining three-quarters of the Upper Peninsula in exchange for giving up the strip, a deal considered poor at the time but whose mineral wealth became an asset.

Source: Wikipedia, 'Toledo War'.
